Set C, the hinge: the 3 cells r2c7, r6c7, r7c7 of column 7 hold only 1, 4, 7 and 9: one digit more than cells. Without any one of these digits, the others fill the cells.
Every 7 of set A sees every 7 of set C: if r2c1 is 7, r2c7 cannot be 7.
If set C holds no 7, its other 3 digits fill its 3 cells, so r6c7 must be 9.
Set B: the 4 cells r1c2, r3c2, r6c2, r9c2 of column 2 hold only 2, 3, 4, 5 and 9: one digit more than cells. Without any one of these digits, the others fill the cells.
Every 9 of set C sees every 9 of set B: if r6c7 is 9, r6c2 cannot be 9.
If set B holds no 9, its other 4 digits fill its 4 cells, so r1c2 must be 5.
Set A or set B holds a 5: if A holds none, B holds one. Each removed 5 sees every 5 of both. So 5 is removed from r1c1.

Petal B, for the stem's 7: the 2 cells r6c3, r6c6 of row 6 hold only 1, 5 and 7: one digit more than cells, and every 7 of it sees the stem.
If the stem is 7, petal B holds no 7, so its other 2 digits fill its 2 cells: r6c6 must be 1.
Whichever digit the stem takes, a petal holds a 1. Each removed 1 sees every 1 of every petal. So 1 is removed from r8c6.
